Get started Continue I understand back Pop quiz! Remote ADB access can expose sensitive data on your device. Leaving ADB enabled when not in use can increase security risks if your device is accessed by an untrusted party. Remote ADB access can reach sensitive information. Only connect to authority nodes you trust, and agree in advance on what they will do. If ADB remains enabled, it may be misused by anyone with physical or network access to your device. Disable ADB immediately after a session. Remote ADB, over the internet MESH lets an authority node you trust connect to your phone, the peer node, with ADB over the internet — only when you say so, and only for as long as you allow. Open-source · independently audited How it works A private link, just for the session MESH builds a direct, end-to-end encrypted connection between your phone (the peer node) and the authority node — nothing in between can read it. End-to-end encrypted with WireGuard Connects peer-to-peer, even behind firewalls or mobile networks The app collects no data and keeps no servers running The link exists only while a session is active You\'re in control Nothing happens without your OK Before a session, agree with whoever runs the authority node on what they will do. With your consent, they may: Read logs and copy files from your phone Install, update or remove apps Run commands and change settings on your phone You decide when access turns on and off. You can end the session in one tap, anytime.

How a session works A session is a temporary, private connection between your phone (the peer node) and an authority node you trust. Here\'s the whole thing, start to finish. You start a session Scan the authority node\'s QR or enter a short code. Nothing connects until you do this. A private link is built Your phone and the authority node connect directly, end-to-end encrypted. No one in between can read it. You stay informed You can watch your connection status live, and the authority node only works within the limits you agreed to beforehand. You end it, anytime One tap tears down the link. Wireless debugging switches back off. Nothing keeps running.
Wireless debugging Let the authority node connect over Wi-Fi This is an Android feature called wireless debugging. Follow these steps once — you can turn it off again as soon as you\'re done. Menu names differ slightly across phones (e.g. \"About phone\" → \"Software information\"). The steps are the same. Only keep wireless debugging on while you\'re connected to the authority node. Turn it off afterwards. Open settings It\'s on Open system Settings Go to Settings → About phone → Software information. Enable Developer options Find \"Build number\" and tap it 7 times. Enter your PIN if asked. Open Developer options Use the button below to jump there, or find it under Settings → System. Turn on Wireless debugging Inside Developer options, switch on \"Wireless debugging\". Come back here Return to MESH and continue your session setup. Wireless debugging requires Android 11 or higher Navigate to System → Developer options → Wireless debugging Unable to open settings. Please enable Wireless debugging manually.
